## Natural history notes

A small deer fly characterized by its compact body, large patterned eyes, short antennae, and clear to dark-banded wings typical of Chrysops flies. In Florida, it is found around wetlands, marshes, swamps, ponds, wet woods, and other humid habitats where larvae can develop in aquatic or semi-aquatic soils and vegetation. Adults are active daytime flies; females seek blood meals from mammals, including livestock, wildlife, and people, while males and females may also visit flowers or feed on plant sugars.
